items.title: CATL signs sodium-battery supply deal for Europe
items.summary: CATL has agreed to supply 5 gigawatt-hours of its newly launched sodium-based TENER storage system to western European markets including the Netherlands starting in 2027. The agreement, formalized through a memorandum of understanding with Dutch energy solutions provider Alfen, is part of CATL's dual-track strategy to push both lithium and sodium chemistries into grid storage.

items.title: Stryten Energy to acquire C&D Technologies and Trojan Battery
items.summary: Stryten Energy has signed a definitive agreement to acquire C&D Technologies and Trojan Battery Co., a deal expected to close in the third quarter of 2026 pending regulatory approval. The combination will create a manufacturer spanning both lead- and lithium-based storage technologies, operating 15 facilities across the US, with Jefferies advising and terms undisclosed.

items.title: Ore Energy signs 1GWh iron-air battery deal in Netherlands
items.summary: Multi-day storage startup Ore Energy has agreed with Dutch utility Budget Thuis to deploy up to 1,000MWh of iron-air batteries, with a 400MWh first phase due for delivery in 2028. The cobalt-free, iron-based technology is designed for 24- to 100-hour discharge durations to store wind power across multiple days.

items.title: Waaree ESS starts 5.15GWh BESS container plant in India
items.summary: Waaree Energy Storage Solutions has begun operations at a battery storage container manufacturing facility in India that was expanded from a planned 3.5GWh to 5.15GWh due to production optimization and higher cell energy density. It represents the first phase of the company's broader 20GWh integrated manufacturing roadmap, which will later add lithium cell and battery pack production lines.

items.title: Global large-scale BESS additions hit 9.1GW/33.5GWh in a month
items.summary: Roughly 9.1GW/33.5GWh of large-scale battery storage came online globally last month, with Saudi Arabia contributing over a third of that new capacity. Separately, Argentina's government awarded 700MW of battery storage in its latest nationwide AlmaSADI tender.

items.title: Max Planck team solves solid-state battery dendrite puzzle
items.summary: Researchers at Germany's Max Planck Institute for Sustainable Materials have identified the mechanical fracture mechanism behind dendrite failure in garnet solid electrolytes, resolving a long-standing debate in battery engineering. The finding, published in Nature and re-highlighted in a July 10 release, opens up several targeted engineering pathways for next-generation EV and consumer batteries.

items.title: China set to release first solid-state EV battery standard
items.summary: China is preparing to finalize its first national standard for solid-state EV batteries in July 2026, following a draft released for public comment covering terminology and classification. The move coincides with several automakers, including Dongfeng, GAC, BYD and Geely, already installing semi-solid-state cells in test vehicles.

items.title: Details emerge on CATL's zero-degradation BESS chemistry
items.summary: New technical details have surfaced on CATL's zero-degradation battery energy storage technology, which the company first announced two years ago and is now advancing toward commercial deployment. The analysis examines how the chemistry aims to eliminate capacity fade over the operating life of grid-scale storage systems.

items.title: INPOW debuts 587Ah semi-solid-state cell at Intersolar
items.summary: GAC Group's energy storage arm INPOW Battery unveiled a 587Ah semi-solid-state cell at Intersolar Europe 2026, alongside a 6.25MWh liquid-cooled utility storage system featuring built-in diagnostics and a triple-layer safety design. The launch was part of a wave of storage product announcements at the trade show from Ampace, Envision and other manufacturers.
